transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Well... I suppose I've just been having a hard time lately. What actually scared me enough to finally come in is that... well, I keep having these mornings. Where I just think... maybe it would be easier if I just didn't wake up. 

I don't have a plan to actually hurt myself or anything like that. I wouldn't do that. But... having those thoughts was enough to make me ask for help, I suppose.
How long have you been having these difficult mornings with thoughts about not waking up?
Well... I suppose it's been about a month. Ever since... well, my sister passed away. It was quite unexpected.
Have you been enjoying things you usually like to do over the past month?

Well... not really, no. I still make myself show up for things, like my book club, or the dance night. But... I just sit there. It feels a bit like I'm behind a pane of glass, I suppose. 

And... even my garden, or cooking for the neighbors... they just don't give me that little lift they used to.
Have you noticed any change in your weight over the past month?

I suppose... maybe a little. I haven't been trying to lose weight or anything. It's just... food doesn't really call to me much anymore. 

I'll fix a little toast, or maybe some soup... and then by evening, I realize I've barely eaten.
Have you noticed any change in your energy level or how quickly you move compared to before your sister passed away?

Yes... I suppose I have. I just feel rather worn out lately. Even just doing simple errands, or... getting the papers together for the Cultural Center. It takes a lot out of me now. It just feels a bit like my body is moving through thick mud, I suppose.
Do you find yourself fidgeting or restless, or do you feel like you're slowing down in your movements compared to how you used to be?
I don't think I'm restless, no. Just... what I mentioned a moment ago. I suppose I'm just a bit slower. I haven't really noticed much else.
Have you been feeling guilty about anything or like you're worthless since your sister passed away?

I suppose... well, yes. I do think about it quite a bit. The last few weeks with her. I just keep going over it in my head, telling myself I should have called more often. Or... or just listened better. Done something more useful. I know, in my head, that I couldn't have changed what happened, but... I still feel like I failed her somehow.
Are there any activities that you still enjoy or find pleasure in?

I... well, I try to keep up with things. I still make myself show up for the book club, or... the dance night. But I don't know, lately I just sit there feeling a bit like I'm behind a pane of glass. And... well, even my garden, or cooking for the neighbors... it just doesn't give me that little lift it used to. So... I suppose not.
Have you been experiencing any difficulty concentrating or making decisions since your sister passed away?

I suppose... yes, a little. I've noticed I'll just stare at the same budgeting spreadsheet for a while. Or... if I'm reading something for a workshop, I might reread a paragraph three or four times. And I still won't really take in what it says. It just doesn't seem to stick.
Have you been feeling like you're moving more slowly than usual or having trouble getting started with activities?

I suppose... yes. I just... I get worn out very easily lately. Even just running simple errands, or... trying to get the papers together for the Cultural Center. It feels a bit like... well, like my body is just moving through thick mud. It takes a lot out of me to get started.
Have you been experiencing these feelings of sadness and emptiness every day since your sister passed away?
Yes... I suppose so. It's been about a month now. Since she... well, since she died. It was very unexpected, so... yes, pretty much every day since then.
Are there any activities that you still find pleasure in or enjoy doing?

Not... not really, no. I mean, I still make myself show up for things. The book club, or... the dance night. But I just sort of sit there. It feels a bit like I'm... behind a pane of glass, I suppose. Even my garden... or cooking for the neighbors. It just doesn't give me that little lift it used to.
Are there any activities that you used to enjoy, but now find you no longer take pleasure in?

Well... like I just mentioned, I suppose it's mostly those things. The gardening, and... cooking for people. I used to really look forward to them. Now... I don't know. I just do them out of habit, but... that feeling of enjoyment just isn't there anymore.
Have you had any days in the past month where you felt somewhat better, or has it been consistently difficult every day?
I suppose... no, not really. It's just been... consistently like this. Every day.
Are there any activities that you still find pleasure in or enjoy doing?

I... I think I just mentioned this a moment ago. No, not really. Like I said, I still make myself go to the book club and the dance night, but... I just sit there feeling like I'm behind a pane of glass. And... even the gardening, or cooking for the neighbors... they just don't give me that lift they used to.
Have you had any thoughts that you would be better off dead, rather than just not waking up?

Well... no. Not exactly that I'd be better off dead. I don't... I don't have any plan to do anything like that. But... I suppose what finally made me come in here is... well, there are mornings where I just think... it might be easier if I just didn't wake up at all.
Have you been feeling restless or fidgety since your sister passed away?
No... I don't think so. I haven't really felt restless or anything like that. I mostly just... sit quietly.
Have you experienced a significant loss of interest in activities you once enjoyed for most of the day, nearly every day?

Yes... I suppose so. Like I mentioned a minute ago, I still show up for the book club and the dances, but I'm just... sitting behind that glass. It's like that most days. The garden and cooking just don't give me any sort of lift anymore.
Do you feel like you're moving more slowly than usual?
No... I don't think so. I haven't noticed anything like that.
Do you feel like your movements have slowed down or sped up since your sister passed away?
I... well, like I just said, no. I haven't noticed my movements changing at all. I'm just... the same, I guess.
